papers.summary: With advances in generative AI, there is now potential for autonomous agents to manage daily tasks via natural language commands. However, current agents are primarily created and tested in simplified synthetic environments, leading to a disconnect with real-world scenarios. In this paper, we build an environment for language-guided agents that is highly realistic and reproducible. Specifically, we focus on agents that perform tasks on the web, and create an environment with fully functional websites from four common domains: e-commerce, social forum discussions, collaborative software development, and content management. Our environment is enriched with tools (e.g., a map) and external knowledge bases (e.g., user manuals) to encourage human-like task-solving. Building upon our environment, we release a set of benchmark tasks focusing on evaluating the functional correctness of task completions. The tasks in our benchmark are diverse, long-horizon, and designed to emulate tasks that humans routinely perform on the internet. We experiment with several baseline agents, integrating recent techniques such as reasoning before acting. The results demonstrate that solving complex tasks is challenging: our best GPT-4-based agent only achieves an end-to-end task success rate of 14.41%, significantly lower than the human performance of 78.24%. These results highlight the need for further development of robust agents, that current state-of-the-art large language models are far from perfect performance in these real-life tasks, and that \ours can be used to measure such progress.\footnote{Code, data, environment reproduction instructions, video demonstrations are available in the supplementary.}

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
papers.authors: Rishabh Agarwal, Nino Vieillard, Zhou, Yongchao, Piotr Stańczyk et al.
papers.what: [Conference] Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used for compressing a teacher model to reduce its inference cost and memory footprint, by training a smaller student model. However, current KD methods for auto-regressive sequence models suffer from distribution mismatch between output sequ
papers.summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used for compressing a teacher model to reduce its inference cost and memory footprint, by training a smaller student model. However, current KD methods for auto-regressive sequence models suffer from distribution mismatch between output sequences seen during training and those generated by the student during inference. To address this issue, we introduce Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Instead of solely relying on a fixed set of output sequences, GKD trains the student on its self-generated output sequences by leveraging feedback from the teacher on such sequences. Unlike supervised KD approaches, GKD also offers the flexibility to employ alternative loss functions between the student and teacher, which can be useful when the student lacks the expressivity to mimic the teacher's distribution. Furthermore, GKD facilitates the seamless integration of distillation with RL fine-tuning (RLHF). We demonstrate the efficacy of GKD for distilling auto-regressive language models on summarization, translation, and arithmetic reasoning tasks, and task-agnostic distillation for instruction-tuning.

papers.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
papers.authors: Lee, Harrison, Samrat Phatale, Mansoor, Hassan, Mesnard, Thomas et al.
papers.what: [Conference] Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has proven effective in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, but gathering high-quality preference labels is expensive. RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF), introduced in Bai et al., offers a promising alternative
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has proven effective in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, but gathering high-quality preference labels is expensive. RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF), introduced in Bai et al., offers a promising alternative that trains the reward model (RM) on preferences generated by an off-the-shelf LLM. Across the tasks of summarization, helpful dialogue generation, and harmless dialogue generation, we show that RLAIF achieves comparable performance to RLHF. Furthermore, we take a step towards "self-improvement" by demonstrating that RLAIF can outperform a supervised fine-tuned baseline even when the AI labeler is the same size as the policy, or even the exact same checkpoint as the initial policy. Finally, we introduce direct-RLAIF (d-RLAIF) - a technique that circumvents RM training by obtaining rewards directly from an off-the-shelf LLM during RL, which achieves superior performance to canonical RLAIF. Our results suggest that RLAIF can achieve performance on-par with using human feedback, offering a potential solution to the scalability limitations of RLHF.

papers.title: CogVideoX: Text-to-Video Diffusion Models with An Expert Transformer
papers.authors: Zhuoyi Yang, Jiayan Teng, Wendi Zheng, Ding, Ming et al.
papers.what: [Conference] We present CogVideoX, a large-scale text-to-video generation model based on diffusion transformer, which can generate 10-second continuous videos aligned with text prompt, with a frame rate of 16 fps and resolution of 768 * 1360 pixels. Previous video generation models often had
papers.summary: We present CogVideoX, a large-scale text-to-video generation model based on diffusion transformer, which can generate 10-second continuous videos aligned with text prompt, with a frame rate of 16 fps and resolution of 768 * 1360 pixels. Previous video generation models often had limited movement and short durations, and is difficult to generate videos with coherent narratives based on text. We propose several designs to address these issues. First, we propose a 3D Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to compress videos along both spatial and temporal dimensions, to improve both compression rate and video fidelity. Second, to improve the text-video alignment, we propose an expert transformer with the expert adaptive LayerNorm to facilitate the deep fusion between the two modalities. Third, by employing a progressive training and multi-resolution frame pack technique, CogVideoX is adept at producing coherent, long-duration, different shape videos characterized by significant motions. In addition, we develop an effective text-video data processing pipeline that includes various data preprocessing strategies and a video captioning method, greatly contributing to the generation quality and semantic alignment. Results show that CogVideoX demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across both multiple machine metrics and human evaluations. The model weight of both 3D Causal VAE, Video caption model and CogVideoX are publicly available at https://github.com/THUDM/CogVideo.

papers.title: DreamGaussian: Generative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Content Creation
papers.authors: Jiaxiang Tang, Jiawei Ren, Hang Zhou, Ziwei Liu et al.
papers.what: [Conference] Recent advances in 3D content creation mostly leverage optimization-based 3D generation via score distillation sampling (SDS). Though promising results have been exhibited, these methods often suffer from slow per-sample optimization, limiting their practical usage. In this paper
papers.summary: Recent advances in 3D content creation mostly leverage optimization-based 3D generation via score distillation sampling (SDS). Though promising results have been exhibited, these methods often suffer from slow per-sample optimization, limiting their practical usage. In this paper, we propose DreamGaussian, a novel 3D content generation framework that achieves both efficiency and quality simultaneously. Our key insight is to design a generative 3D Gaussian Splatting model with companioned mesh extraction and texture refinement in UV space. In contrast to the occupancy pruning used in Neural Radiance Fields, we demonstrate that the progressive densification of 3D Gaussians converges significantly faster for 3D generative tasks. To further enhance the texture quality and facilitate downstream applications, we introduce an efficient algorithm to convert 3D Gaussians into textured meshes and apply a fine-tuning stage to refine the details. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior efficiency and competitive generation quality of our proposed approach. Notably, DreamGaussian produces high-quality textured meshes in just 2 minutes from a single-view image, achieving approximately 10 times acceleration compared to existing methods.

papers.title: SALMONN: Towards Generic Hearing Abilities for Large Language Models
papers.authors: Changli Tang, Wenyi Yu, Guangzhi Sun, Xianzhao Chen et al.
papers.what: [Conference] Hearing is arguably an essential ability of artificial intelligence (AI) agents in the physical world, which refers to the perception and understanding of general auditory information consisting of at least three types of sounds: speech, audio events, and music. In this paper, we
papers.summary: Hearing is arguably an essential ability of artificial intelligence (AI) agents in the physical world, which refers to the perception and understanding of general auditory information consisting of at least three types of sounds: speech, audio events, and music. In this paper, we propose SALMONN, a speech audio language music open neural network, built by integrating a pre-trained text-based large language model (LLM) with speech and audio encoders into a single multimodal model. SALMONN enables the LLM to directly process and understand general audio inputs and achieve competitive performances on a number of speech and audio tasks used in training, such as automatic speech recognition and translation, auditory-information-based question answering, emotion recognition, speaker verification, and music and audio captioning etc. SALMONN also has a diverse set of emergent abilities unseen in the training, which includes but is not limited to speech translation to untrained languages, speech-based slot filling, spoken-query-based question answering, audio-based storytelling, and speech audio co-reasoning etc. The presence of cross-modal emergent abilities is studied, and a novel few-shot activation tuning approach is proposed to activate such abilities. To our knowledge, SALMONN is the first model of its type and can be regarded as a step towards AI with generic hearing abilities. The source code, model checkpoints and data are available at https://github.com/bytedance/SALMONN.

papers.title: MyMuse: A Personal Museum for Post-Visit Inquiry and Reflection
papers.authors: Jiyeon Bae, Chunggi Lee, Jinwook Seo, Hanspeter Pfister
papers.what: [Explore] Artwork photographs may preserve what visitors saw without preserving why it mattered. Revisiting them can involve recalling earlier responses and developing new questions and interpretations as knowledge and personal experiences change. Yet recurring interests may remain difficu
papers.summary: Artwork photographs may preserve what visitors saw without preserving why it mattered. Revisiting them can involve recalling earlier responses and developing new questions and interpretations as knowledge and personal experiences change. Yet recurring interests may remain difficult to recognize across individual exchanges. Informed by a formative study with ten visitors, we present MyMuse, a post-visit system that connects inquiry about individual artworks with reflection across visitors' accumulated records. In its Personal Museum, visitors revisit artworks, ask questions, and record interpretations that inform subsequent system responses. Its interactive Narrative Report reorganizes the same records across artworks through four interpretive lenses. In two within-subject studies with 16 participants, direct comparisons favored MyMuse for vivid revisitation. The report received higher ratings for recurring-interest awareness, cross-artwork connections, and unexpected discovery than a per-artwork presentation of the same records. These findings suggest that examining accumulated records can support reflection on recurring interests and relationships among visitors' responses across artworks.

papers.title: Explaining intersectional segregation in multi-attribute social networks
papers.authors: Clara Eminente, Elisa Omodei, Michele Starnini
papers.what: [Explore] Segregation in students' friendships shapes their access to information and opportunities, and schools can reduce it by setting the composition of their classes. Yet segregation is usually measured one attribute at a time, although attributes such as migration background and sex
papers.summary: Segregation in students' friendships shapes their access to information and opportunities, and schools can reduce it by setting the composition of their classes. Yet segregation is usually measured one attribute at a time, although attributes such as migration background and sex are often correlated, so a preference over one can create segregation on the other. A single-attribute reading then attributes this induced segregation to the wrong preference and cannot identify which part of it a school can remove. In a network model with preferences over two correlated attributes, we derive in closed form the Coleman index, a standard segregation measure, separating the segregation due to each preference from the segregation it induces on the other attribute. In friendship networks of school classes in four European countries, ignoring sex inflates the estimated preference over migration background, increasingly so as the two attributes are more correlated. The closed form also shows what class composition can achieve. When students have no preference over one attribute, the segregation induced on it can be removed, whereas segregation set by a homophilic preference over the other cannot be changed. When both preferences are active, splitting a school with equal-sized groups and independent attributes reduces segregation only if the preferences pull in opposite directions. Judging a split by the school-wide average can hide classes that become more segregated. In the data, the split derived from the closed form removes induced segregation, and splitting does not lower segregation where both preferences are homophilic, as predicted.

papers.title: How Fast Stored Household Assignments Go Stale: Evidence from North Carolina Voter Rolls
papers.authors: Prashant Chaudhary
papers.what: [Explore] Household files and identity graphs are judged by whether they still find the person. That test misses what they store. A household assignment can go stale while every person-level link in it stays right, because the people around the person change. We measure how fast, for house
papers.summary: Household files and identity graphs are judged by whether they still find the person. That test misses what they store. A household assignment can go stale while every person-level link in it stays right, because the people around the person change. We measure how fast, for households derived from a voter register, by following North Carolina registrants on a persistent identifier across 40 distinct snapshots from November 2008 to November 2026 (3.6 million clients at the 2016 build in 60 counties). Eight years after the 2016 build, the graph finds the address of 0.831 of registrants still listed, yet its household is exactly right for only 0.322 of those found (0.309 reading stale listings as departures). A mover's stored household is right about one time in five at every build from two to eight years, so the loss runs through who stays and how households that stay change. Stricter thresholds of a probabilistic name-and-address matcher raise accuracy only to about the stayers' currency, mainly by selecting stayers. Lookup tables of currency by build-time features cut Brier score by 16% to 19% against evidence age alone and 6% to 10% against evidence age and household size, on held-out counties and a later file. A multistate model of household change does not beat a table with the same inputs, and the tables choose which quarter of a file to refresh no better than evidence age and household size do. In Ohio and Washington at eight to nine years the tables keep their ranking after an in-sample intercept shift; the accounting's level holds in Washington and not in Ohio. Simulated build error of 5% to 21% costs 2% to 10% of eight-year currency.

papers.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
papers.authors: Hanzhao Xi, Zhonghao Li, Suxuan Liu, Shanghan Zhou et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps.
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared Assembly Intermediate Representation (Assembly IR). PlanRefine audits PartGround assignments against finite inventory by removing the lowest-confidence assignments. Uncertain identity cases remain marked for review in the Assembly IR. We evaluate CAPER on the IKEA Assembly in the Wild (IAW) dataset. Experiment results show that CAPER reaches a Finite-inventory Consistency Rate of 83.33% and produces zero observed out-of-inventory Part-ID occurrences. At the plan level, PlanRefine removes all observed inventory-overuse pairs (9 -> 0) and excess units (51 -> 0). Overall, the results indicate that PartGround and PlanRefine improve part reliability, while also enhancing finite-inventory consistency and local prediction accuracy. Project page and video: https://xhzzzz123.github.io/CAPER/

papers.title: Sound Distributed Runtime Verification under Incomplete Evidence
papers.authors: Nikolaos Kekatos, Antonio Anastasio Bruto da Costa, Alexios Lekidis, Pabitra Mitra et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Distributed runtime verification often requires combining evidence from several nodes to check properties that cannot be evaluated locally. However, when messages are delayed, lost, or deliberately suppressed, the verifier may not know whether a violation occurred or whether the
papers.summary: Distributed runtime verification often requires combining evidence from several nodes to check properties that cannot be evaluated locally. However, when messages are delayed, lost, or deliberately suppressed, the verifier may not know whether a violation occurred or whether the relevant evidence is missing. This creates a risk of incorrectly reporting compliance. We study the requirements for sound monitoring under these conditions. We first show that a deadline-bounded monitor cannot be simultaneously sound, decisive, and available when an adversary can suppress evidence. The monitor must therefore be able to abstain. We then distinguish two sources of incomplete evidence. Sequence numbers and periodic reports can identify missing events, whereas detecting silent streams requires timing assumptions. We also examine how membership changes and coordinator failures affect verdict soundness and recovery. We implement these mechanisms in a three-tier monitoring architecture using MQTT and NATS JetStream. Experiments with an LLM-planned robot swarm demonstrate the failure modes, show how the proposed mechanisms prevent unsupported compliance verdicts, and measure their runtime and communication costs.

papers.title: Network topology imposes spectral constraints on collective nonequilibrium responses
papers.authors: Dingjie Wu, Yaozu Wang, Rong Wang, Ying Wu
papers.what: [Explore] Collective nonequilibrium dynamics in Langevin systems depend on both network topology and stochastic driving. Understanding the role of topology in responses to stochastic driving and in the emergence of nonequilibrium is essential. Starting from the principle of microscopic rev
papers.summary: Collective nonequilibrium dynamics in Langevin systems depend on both network topology and stochastic driving. Understanding the role of topology in responses to stochastic driving and in the emergence of nonequilibrium is essential. Starting from the principle of microscopic reversibility and linear Langevin dynamics on networks, we derive a mode decomposition for both the asymmetry of short-time cross-correlations and heat currents at steady state. This decomposition reveals two sources of nonequilibrium---fluctuations of individual modes and correlated fluctuations between distinct modes. For reciprocal networks with independent local driving, we derive two nonequilibrium response operators that yield explicit expressions for the global asymmetry intensity and the entropy production rate. These operators are weighted Laplacians independent of stochastic driving. Their spectra determine attainable upper and lower bounds on nonequilibrium at fixed driving heterogeneity. These bounds are exact for asymmetry intensity at arbitrary deviations from equilibrium and hold to leading order near equilibrium for entropy production rate. Finally, we find that the hierarchical modular organization of human structural connectomes broadens the brain's nonequilibrium operating range, with resting-state brain activity supporting this topological advantage for sustaining a lower nonequilibrium level. Our study provides a basis for understanding biological network organization and designing networks with targeted nonequilibrium operating points.

papers.title: A Bernstein-Type Variance-Adaptive PMW Mechanism for DP Query Release
papers.authors: Mohamed Aniss Benstaali, Habib Louafi, Naima Bessah
papers.what: [Explore] Private Multiplicative Weights (PMW) is a central mechanism for the differentially private release of adaptive linear statistics over a finite universe. Its classical analysis uses a fixed multiplicative-weights learning rate and does not exploit the local variance of the current
papers.summary: Private Multiplicative Weights (PMW) is a central mechanism for the differentially private release of adaptive linear statistics over a finite universe. Its classical analysis uses a fixed multiplicative-weights learning rate and does not exploit the local variance of the current hypothesis. This paper presents PMW-Bernstein, a variance-adaptive refinement in which the update step is determined by the relationship between the privately estimated query error and the variance under the current hypothesis. The mechanism retains the standard PMW privacy architecture based on Sparse Vector screening, Gaussian numerical measurements, sequential composition, and post-processing. Through a potential-based analysis, we prove a one-step progress bound that yields a global weighted energy bound, recovers the classical $O(1/α2)$ update regime in general, and establishes an $O(1/α)$ update regime under a Bernsteintype condition on updated rounds. Controlled simulations over synthetic finite-universe distributions and query workloads show that the adaptive rule reduces the number of updates in the low-variance regime, remains competitive in the high-variance regime, and succeeds within the prescribed update budget in the heterogeneous regime where the fixed-step baseline fails.

papers.title: PORTA: Systematic Discovery of Vulnerabilities in Identity Brokers
papers.authors: Zixu Zhou, Xiangyu Guo, Ilya Grishchenko, David Lie
papers.what: [Explore] Identity brokers such as Keycloak, Vault, and Dex translate authentication proofs from an upstream identity provider into sessions for downstream services. Due to their central role in authentication and trust mediation, a single vulnerability in a broker compromises every downst
papers.summary: Identity brokers such as Keycloak, Vault, and Dex translate authentication proofs from an upstream identity provider into sessions for downstream services. Due to their central role in authentication and trust mediation, a single vulnerability in a broker compromises every downstream service behind it. In fact, recent incidents have demonstrated that even widely adopted platforms are not immune to such issues, highlighting the critical need for systematic analysis. To build such an analysis, this work first defines invariants for broker operation. These invariants are not completely covered by existing authentication specifications, primarily because brokers are unique in their duality, i.e., acting simultaneously as a relying party and an identity provider. The invariants capture the properties that identity brokers must uphold throughout their workflows, as all 60 previous CVEs we consider violate at least one invariant. Within these workflows, we further define high-level action categories. Equipped with this information, our automated tool PORTA leverages a large language model (LLM) to generate API invocation sequences corresponding to the high-level action categories, and oracle assertions aligned with the specified invariants. PORTA identifies 33 previously unreported security vulnerabilities in seven popular open-source brokers. We study these novel vulnerabilities and trace them to eight recurring patterns. We responsibly disclosed all discovered vulnerabilities: 29 have been confirmed, 14 patched, and 19 assigned CVE numbers, with 10 CVEs rated as critical.

papers.title: Protective-Design Pre-Emption in Child-Facing Generative AI
papers.authors: Verena Jasmin Hallitschke, Mahelie Dissanayake, Elisa Nguyen
papers.what: [Explore] Generative AI is adopted rapidly by children, yet unrestricted general-audience models dominate their usage. This paper presents the open problem of \emph{protective-design pre-emption}: Delayed market introduction, low access thresholds, utility gaps, habituation, and peer adopt
papers.summary: Generative AI is adopted rapidly by children, yet unrestricted general-audience models dominate their usage. This paper presents the open problem of \emph{protective-design pre-emption}: Delayed market introduction, low access thresholds, utility gaps, habituation, and peer adoption foster unrestricted AI model lock-in, leading children to bypass child-centric platforms. With first signs of lower adoption of child-centric platforms, we argue that this shift may reinforce existing AI risks such as exposing children to deepened parasocial dependencies, skill erosion, and misinformation. To address this problem, we propose interdisciplinary research directions to quantify pre-emption, understand its socio-technical drivers, and develop interventions ensuring child-centric AI is actively adopted, not just available.

papers.title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens
papers.authors: Yi-Jun Chen, I-Tsen Hsieh, Li-Wun Chang
papers.what: [Explore] Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited. This s
papers.summary: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited. This study examined how supportive versus challenging chatbot interaction styles shape user experience and continuance intention, and whether people-pleasing tendency (PPT) moderates these effects across cultures. Taiwanese (N = 49) and Korean (N = 52) participants completed a collaborative tourism-planning task. Results showed that: (1) supportive chatbots consistently led to higher continuance intention, satisfaction, and trust; (2) PPT did not moderate these effects; and (3) cultural variation emerged only in perceived threat, where higher PPT was associated with greater baseline threat in the Taiwanese but not the Korean sample. These findings reveal how a general-purpose LLM style may differentially activate culturally situated social scripts, raising implications for culturally inclusive conversational AI design.

papers.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
papers.authors: Feng Yu
papers.what: [Explore] In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demog
papers.summary: In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demographic models. This paper proposes that the ubiquity of mobile internet and Artificial Intelligence acts as a synthetic mating disruptor, precipitating a non-linear phase transition in human pair-bonding dynamics. Treating the marriage market as a complex system governed by thermodynamic constraints, we present a Fermi-Dirac selection model, using national income distributions as the input spectrum and fitted with Japanese longitudinal data to illustrate how digital hyper-reality generates an increasingly prohibitive Marriage Energy Barrier. Our model quantifies a Tech Factor that decouples female mating expectations from local economic realities during initial courtship, a distortion we predict will be severely exacerbated as AI evolves into an emotional substitute. Projections indicate that this substitution effect is accelerating; without intervention, the world post 2040 risks entering an irreversible demographic contraction, as the sudden surge in TFR required for recovery is biologically impossible. Ultimately, this framework explains why traditional financial subsidies fail to reverse falling birth rates and suggests that digital convenience may represent a behavioral Great Filter that erodes the imperative for species persistence.

papers.title: Found in Translation: Five Entry Points to Translate AI Literacy Frameworks in the Design of Educational Materials
papers.authors: Luis Morales-Navarro, Karl-Emil K. Bilstrup, Mille Skovhus Lunding, Luke Connelly et al.
papers.what: [Explore] While there is a plethora of AI literacy and informatics frameworks, in practice it is difficult for designers of educational materials and educators to decide where to start and how to use these in learning activities. At the same time, recent reviews show that despite the fact
papers.summary: While there is a plethora of AI literacy and informatics frameworks, in practice it is difficult for designers of educational materials and educators to decide where to start and how to use these in learning activities. At the same time, recent reviews show that despite the fact that most frameworks emphasize the socio-technical nature of AI, in practice interventions tend to center on preparing learners to use AI. To address these issues, we ask: How can multiple stakeholders negotiate and translate AI literacy framework ideas into common language that can be used to design introductory learning materials for primary school children, teachers and parents? We introduce five entry points into AI literacy that were developed from a computational empowerment perspective through a participatory design process involving primary teacher educators, curricular designers, media producers, and researchers. We present three vignettes that illustrate how the entry points were generative in the design of learning activities, learning tools and media content for school and home. This paper contributes an account of the participatory development of five entry points that serve as generative and negotiable resources for designing educational materials.

papers.title: Interaction dynamics of the 'Friends'
papers.authors: Shun Zhang, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Christopher M. Danforth, Peter Sheridan Dodds
papers.what: [Explore] Computational narrative analysis increasingly seeks representations that capture how language reflects changing social and interactional contexts. We apply Ousiometry, a lexicon-based framework organized around Power, Danger, and Structure, to the complete dialogue of Friends (23
papers.summary: Computational narrative analysis increasingly seeks representations that capture how language reflects changing social and interactional contexts. We apply Ousiometry, a lexicon-based framework organized around Power, Danger, and Structure, to the complete dialogue of Friends (236 episodes, 750K tokens), examining temporal variation, group-level positioning, and pairwise co-variation among the six main characters. We find substantial episode-to-episode fluctuation in character trajectories, with PELT-detected change points descriptively aligning with major narrative events. At the group level, character combinations occupy different regions of Power--Danger space, with greater dispersion in Power than Danger, although these differences do not survive Bonferroni correction and trajectory clustering shows weak structure (silhouette = 0.27). Pairwise Pearson correlations reveal modest co-variation across characters, with three significant pairs in Power, two in Danger, and six in Structure after correction. Partial correlations substantially reduce these associations, leaving only one significant pair in Power and one in Danger, suggesting that much of the observed co-variation reflects ensemble-wide rather than pair-specific dynamics. Overall, our findings show that episode-level Ousiometry captures meaningful temporal variation in character dialogue, while evidence for stable group-level structure and pair-specific co-variation remains limited. Semantic variation in Friends is therefore better characterized as continuous and context-dependent.

papers.title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
papers.authors: Jian Li, Qinglin Zhao, Shuoyao Wang, Jincheng Cai et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independen
papers.summary: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers. Since real costs are not public, we measure on synthetic firms with known values how much an honest-but-curious provider recovers when it knows the disguise algorithm, holds sector-level price and margin statistics, and links a firm's queries. In one prompt, per-field scaling, a fixed-axis instantiation of Zhang et al.'s order-preserving substitution and Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt's released sanitizer keep the attacker's margin-hit advantage over a prior-only guess between -0.6 and +4.4 percentage points. After 16 linked queries with fresh secrets, every disguise we test (Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon\geq 0.5$) has a target recovered significantly more often: under the order-preserving substitution, margin recovery rises from 25.0% to 59.4%. The same attacker recovers 29.4 percentage points more margins with fresh maps than with one reused map. Theory explains the contrast: one reused secret bounds all queries by a single full-precision view of the fields shown, whereas fresh scaling keys are identifiable. Except for Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon=0.5$, the gains persist when the attacker's prior comes from another population model and when values drift by up to 5% between queries; on our firms, whose prose cues are weak, reading the prose with a language model adds at most 2.5 points. Code and data: https://github.com/Jamli58/fresh-keys-stale-secrets
